description: La Boheme de Marigny is an authentic 1800s Creole cottage in the hip Marigny neighborhood. host_about: I am a New York transplant (dis-occupying Wall Street) in 2008 and joining Teach for America to teach high school math in inner-city public schools. I am now in my fifteenth year of teaching between my home state of Hawaii, and my adopted homes in New York City and New Orleans.  On school days I am gone by 6 am and generally not back until 5 pm. I either work or travel most weekends. I am a low key and low touch host- but promise to be as accommodating as possible. I try to live as simply and lightly on this earth as possible and hope that my guests will do the same. My home is in a wonderful location, clean, comfortable, and quiet but updated, upscale or fancy.  After a decade in the hospitality business (which supports teaching in high-need public schools) I am reasonably experienced. name: Musical & cultural extravaganza!
description: Location, location, location! The Faubourg Marigny is a neighborhood located adjacent to the French Quarter.  Frenchmen Street, is the destination for some great music!    Lined with music clubs, a couple of restaurants, cafe's, two night time art markets, a great book store, a bicycle shop and small grocery store, it is  just a gateway to many attractions.   Staying in this apartment gives you a huge balcony with a  bird's eye view of the festivities below, people watching at it's finest.
host_about:
I was in the travel business for twenty years before settling down on Frenchmen Street.  As a travel agent I came to know what most people wanted when they travelled, and that is a comfortable & clean bed, a great location and at a price you could afford.  With the airlines limiting what you can bring on board, I stocked the units with everything you might need! 
Bathrobes, toiletries, expresso maker, coffee grinder! Too numerous to mention, it has everything.  And the LOCATION is just great, with crime at all time high, this place is ground zero for the local music scene and with that comes a lot of people which in one way deters crime.  Also, the Frenchmen St Art market is open in the evenings from 7pm to 1am.  we are just two blocks from the quarter so, the whole area is great for walking.  I give it a ten (walkability).  I am here to be your guide, not intrusively, but when and if you need me, I am here as your concierge.  I am Ecuadorian by birth but a native New Orleanian by heart and I love living & hosting in the Marigny and have been doing this for the last 20 years!

name: Marigny Triangle Artist Home
description: Live in the heart of the Marigny Triangle! Just 2 blocks to the French Quarter and Frenchmen St. is our two story guesthouse filled with artistic touches, old New Orleans Storyville charm, with a balcony overlooking our garden courtyard. It was built in the 1850s, with historic home character, vintage aesthetic and New Orleans brick dust. It is behind the main house, seculded and quiet. Perfect for a couple, Sleeps up to 4. OPEN CONCEPT Strict cancellation policy observed. No private parking
host_about:
We are two music professionals who love our city and are happy to share it with fellow travelers. Our home and neighborhood are very unique, the Marigny is the bohemia of New Orleans. Participating in AirBandB helps us restore our 100+ year old home and share its history with others. We are travelers and craftspeople, self employed. You may hear music being played on the property. We can peruse our creativity because of guests coming to stay in our home, so thanks! We present an off beat authentic New Orleans locals life-stlye here, not a corporate run hotel. We value character and authenticity, and open minded adventurers. If that sounds right for you, please come stay!

When we decided to add our home to Airbnb we wanted to make sure that our listings represented what we love about New Orleans. A city full of character, celebration of life, and vibrancy. The exposed brick, bright colors and architecture are some of these aspects.  Sitting in the courtyard  at night is so peaceful, and you can even sometimes faintly hear the brass bands playing on Frenchmen St. We love our city and we hope you will too.

name: HISTORIC ART LOFT near French Quarter & FRENCHMEN!
description:
Stay in a home as unique as New Orleans itself, just steps from the French Quarter. Built nearly 200 years ago for a free woman of color, it's lived many lives—once a Blacksmith’s shop, then post-Katrina blight and the site of the first "Before I Die" installation. Super-fast WiFi, multiple workspaces, walkable streets & easy parking.

License #23-XSTR-11265
host_about:
Professional Artist, Thoughtful Host and Respectful Traveler

As a citizen of the world, I openly welcome guests from all backgrounds. I speak English and Spanish fluently and French and Italian hopefully. :) I pay my staff living wages as well as equal pay for equal work in support of gender equality.

You are staying in a piece of history. This home was originally built for a free woman of color nearly 200 years ago. We found it in total ruin, on the verge of collapse. It was love at first sight!

During the renovation, we supported the use of the home as an art installation. It was to become the original “Before I Die” house. We spent years meticulously rebuilding the home, much of it with our own hands. Now, the property has been reborn as Marigny 9.

We split our time between New Orleans and Sayulita, Mexico. We are so happy to be able to share this magical place with you.

description:

host_about:
“The first thing you notice about New Orleans are the burying grounds - the cemeteries - and they're a cold proposition, one of the best things there are here. Going by, you try to be as quiet as possible, better to let them sleep. Greek, Roman, sepulchres- palatial mausoleums made to order, phantomesque, signs and symbols of hidden decay - ghosts of women and men who have sinned and who've died and are now living in tombs. The past doesn't pass away so quickly here. You could be dead for a long time.

The ghosts race towards the light, you can almost hear the heavy breathing spirits, all determined to get somewhere. New Orleans, unlike a lot of those places you go back to and that don't have the magic anymore, still has got it. Night can swallow you up, yet none of it touches you. Around any corner, there's a promise of something daring and ideal and things are just getting going. There's something obscenely joyful behind every door, either that or somebody crying with their head in their hands. A lazy rhythm looms in the dreamy air and the atmosphere pulsates with bygone duels, past-life romance, comrades requesting comrades to aid them in some way. You can't see it, but you know it's here. Somebody is always sinking. Everyone seems to be from some very old Southern families. Either that or a foreigner. I like the way it is.

There are a lot of places I like, but I like New Orleans better. There's a thousand different angles at any moment. At any time you could run into a ritual honoring some vaguely known queen. Bluebloods, titled persons like crazy drunks, lean weakly against the walls and drag themselves through the gutter. Even they seem to have insights you might want to listen to. No action seems inappropriate here. The city is one very long poem. Gardens full of pansies, pink petunias, opiates. Flower-bedecked shrines, white myrtles, bougainvillea and purple oleander stimulate your senses, make you feel cool and clear inside.

Everything in New Orleans is a good idea. Bijou temple-type cottages and lyric cathedrals side by side. Houses and mansions, structures of wild grace. Italianate, Gothic, Romanesque, Greek Revival standing in a long line in the rain. Roman Catholic art. Sweeping front porches, turrets, cast-iron balconies, colonnades- 30-foot columns, gloriously beautiful- double pitched roofs, all the architecture of the whole wide world and it doesn't move. All that and a town square where public executions took place. In New Orleans you could almost see other dimensions. There's only one day at a time here, then it's tonight and then tomorrow will be today again. Chronic melancholia hanging from the trees. You never get tired of it. After a while you start to feel like a ghost from one of the tombs, like you're in a wax museum below crimson clouds. Spirit empire. Wealthy empire. One of Napoleon's generals, Lallemaud, was said to have come here to check it out, looking for a place for his commander to seek refuge after Waterloo. He scouted around and left, said that here the devil is damned, just like everybody else, only worse. The devil comes here and sighs. New Orleans. Exquisite, old-fashioned. A great place to live vicariously. Nothing makes any difference and you never feel hurt, a great place to really hit on things. Somebody puts something in front of you here and you might as well drink it. Great place to be intimate or do nothing. A place to come and hope you'll get smart - to feed pigeons looking for handouts” bob dylan

host_about:
Folwell Dunbar: An Abridged (and slightly fictitious) Autobiography 

Fol·well \ fόl-wel \ n, pl. Folwells [from the Cajun Faux and Weeeeeee] This highly endangered and elusive species (folwellius dunbarian, estimated population: 1. Common names include Foz, Fu, Fuzzy, Foly and Fu-Bear) was first discovered in the mid 1960s along the creosote shores of Bayou Bonfuca. Genetic research has shown that it was first conceived in Mexico, carried north by a band of Olmec nomads and finally deposited beneath a bald cypress tree in the Honey Island Swamp. Legend has it that an osprey had landed there with a cottonmouth in its talons. The young child was then placed in a pirogue and set adrift. He was soon discovered by a den of aquatic reptilian royalty and nursed to maturity by a particularly handsome, nine-foot she-gator. Once weaned, the young Folwell began feeding on “nutra rats,” water hyacinth and other vile, invasive species. Eventually, the young hominid left its adopted home and sojourned northward to the glaciated reaches of Massachusetts for some good, wholesome Puritanical book learnin. After four frostbitten years of preppy, intellectual enlightenment, Folwell carpetbagged it back south to the gothic tobacco barns of Durham, North Carolina. After another “cough, cough,” four years of higher order thinking and lower order wrestling at Duke University, he ventured to the hinterlands of South America. In Zhumar, Ecuador (pop. 54 on a good day!), he culled rogue sheep, raised rainbow trout in earthen ponds, cooked guinea pigs over an open fire, kept “killer” bees, and drank lots of spittle-tainted chicha and kerosene-toxic trago. Once again though, after almost three years of Andean bliss and Atawalpa’s revenge, the wander-lustful neotropical migrant set off. He trekked along the Ruta Maya, past the land of United Fruit and through the fields of the Zapatistas, until he finally settled in the true “Banana Republic” of Louisiana. In the Big Queasy, he taught Ancient, US and World History, Spanish and First Grade. He studied at Tulane and juggled on Decatur Street, until, once again, he took flight. Landing in the virtual reality of the Research Triangle Park, he helped found a school for techno-savvy cyber children, coached wrestling, and visited countless, generic shopping malls. After only two years in CARY (Concentrated Area of Relocated Yankees), he was drawn back to the Big Queasy by the ethereal beat of Satchmo, Sidney Bichet, and of course Professor Longhair. There, he set out on a quest for comprehensive whole-school reform, a.k.a. Peace Corps with a paycheck. He scooped and delivered dollops of PD, scribbled reams of educational, jargon-infused drivel, and beat the drum loudly for improved teaching and learning.   Folwell, his wife Lucia, and their shaggy and occasionally obedient black dog live in an ancient and decrepit shotgun doublewide, two blocks from Desire (of Streetcar fame), a levee away from Old Man River, and a hop, a skip and a short stagger from the Vieux Carre’. They can be found fighting the stupids, social working, and generally barking around…

Easy going and eager to meet you! 

You will be in good hands when you stay here. My travel and unique life experiences have taught us how to make you comfortable while traveling. In 2009 we quit our day jobs, and spent the next for 2.5 years traveling full time. Landing in Miami, Florida in February of 2012, we hosted many in our tiny Condo. We moved to New Orleans in October of 2015 and spent the first year and a half renovating a dream home in this magical city and love it more and more every year. We look forward to sharing all this greatness with you!

In almost a decade of extensive travel, we've built many friendships, discovered and learned more about ourselves, people and the world than we ever could have imagined. 

We have great history of hosting people in our temporary homes throughout the US and world. We use Air BnB, and other websites/organizations to facilitate these guests. We enjoy Air BnB, and offer do our best to offer guests a great experience.

If you're interested in business and entrepreneurship, you will enjoy staying with us. Ask about our company Elektra Cosmetics, where our mission is to empower people by inspiring a community to be unapologetically creative. Through support, education and quality products we spread the joy of creativity. It has been exciting as we work to develop and grow our business. Just look up Elektra Cosmetics using your favorite search engine or social media platform to learn more.

We love utilizing technology for learning, exploring, researching, completing tasks, and keeping in touch with friends and family.

We love all types food :). We are not foodies, just love trying new cuisines and restaurants. We try not to overindulge, but sharing conversation over a nice meal is always very nice.

We enjoy experiencing the sights and sounds of new locations and are still learning about our great city, New Orleans! We have been on numerous walking and biking tours, and have walked many miles in each place we visit. We look forward to many more enjoyable walks in around our home we hope you can join us for a few.
Danielle-  I am a Certified Orthotist I specialize in designing and fitting helmets on infants with positional plagiocephaly...a condition where a baby's head is becomes abnormally flat from pressure. 

Danielle- My interests are decorating, exploring New Orleans, food, costumes, history, thrifting, vintage, art & adventure, and last but not least,  I love burlesque!!!! name: The Townhouse on Magazine  (Lower Garden District)
description: The Townhouse.  Once, a Jazz Age Speakeasy hidden in an 1850's home on Magazine Street. Built in the Lower Garden District in the time of Mark Twain and riverboats, later pouring Gin while Louis Armstrong was king. Today, a luxury New Orleans pied-à-terre. Original architectural decadence paired with modern style, high ceiling and grand scale. Private walled courtyard. Walk to famous Restaurants, Bars, Shopping, Streetcar, Convention Center, WWII Museum. Closest historic neighborhood to Quarter.
host_about:
I was born in New Orleans and raised in the French Quarter. My father moved from his native London as a professional Jazz musician and started his family at this epicenter of fantastic architecture,  amazing food and renowned music. A childhood like that tends to make a permanent impression so after studying architecture and design in college I worked around the country but was drawn back to this wonderful sticky hot magical city. Moving back I realized just how many amazing historic homes in this city were being forgotten and lost. I started on just one project, one house, but it turned out to just be the "first house". I fell in love with a guy who had the same shared passion for design and preservation and now with our daughter in tow, our family  works relentlesly on acquiring and restoring historic architecture. So far we've restored more than a dozen virtually lost houses (mostly in the LGD) and have no plans to stop anytime soon. Almost all of the houses we have brought back were abandoned, partially collapsed "basket cases" (some even had huge trees growing through their roofs). Often it seems the worse they are, the more we want them.  Their former beauty shines through and their history speaks to us.
 You see, we think that the history and romanticism of New Orleans is best conveyed through the preservation and use of its unique architecture, cooking it's amazing food,  and playing it's fantastic music. And well, since we can't boil water or play a single instrument between us, we've decided to concentrate on the houses. We hope you like what we've done; it wasn't easy. You never know, maybe our daughter will grow up to be a chef who plays the clarinet.

name: 2 Floor 1855 Townhouse Suite Lower Garden District
description: The Townhouse Suite. Once part of a speakeasy, hidden in an 1850's home on Magazine Street, now a luxury New Orleans pied-à-terre. Original architectural decadence paired with modern style, high ceilings and grand scale on two floors with a master bedroom loft and an original wrought iron gallery. Walk to famous Restaurants, Boutiques, Bars and Streetcar. French Quarter, Convention Center, WWII Museum just down the street.
host_about:
I was born in New Orleans and raised in the French Quarter. My father moved from his native London as a professional Jazz musician and started his family at this epicenter of fantastic architecture,  amazing food and renowned music. A childhood like that tends to make a permanent impression so after studying architecture and design in college I worked around the country but was drawn back to this wonderful sticky hot magical city. Moving back I realized just how many amazing historic homes in this city were being forgotten and lost. I started on just one project, one house, but it turned out to just be the "first house". I fell in love with a guy who had the same shared passion for design and preservation and now with our daughter in tow, our family  works relentlesly on acquiring and restoring historic architecture. So far we've restored more than a dozen virtually lost houses (mostly in the LGD) and have no plans to stop anytime soon. Almost all of the houses we have brought back were abandoned, partially collapsed "basket cases" (some even had huge trees growing through their roofs). Often it seems the worse they are, the more we want them.  Their former beauty shines through and their history speaks to us.
 You see, we think that the history and romanticism of New Orleans is best conveyed through the preservation and use of its unique architecture, cooking it's amazing food,  and playing it's fantastic music. name: The Library 2 Bed Suite Lower Garden District
description: Your pied-à-terre in our 1850's townhouse perfectly situated in the walkable Lower Garden District on famous Magazine Street.  Comprising the original 2nd floor library (main bedroom) and then additional rear quarters of the main house with a lovely queen size, sleeping nook-“it feels like the sleeping compartment on an old luxury train” . Kitchenette bar, floor to ceiling windows, exposed brick, old decorative fireplaces, hardwood floors and even a private gallery overlooking a courtyard.
host_about:
I was born in New Orleans and raised in the French Quarter. My father moved from his native London as a professional Jazz musician and started his family at this epicenter of fantastic architecture,  amazing food and renowned music. A childhood like that tends to make a permanent impression so after studying architecture and design in college I worked around the country but was drawn back to this wonderful sticky hot magical city. Moving back I realized just how many amazing historic homes in this city were being forgotten and lost. I started on just one project, one house, but it turned out to just be the "first house". I fell in love with a guy who had the same shared passion for design and preservation and now with our daughter in tow, our family  works relentlesly on acquiring and restoring historic architecture. So far we've restored more than a dozen virtually lost houses (mostly in the LGD) and have no plans to stop anytime soon. Almost all of the houses we have brought back were abandoned, partially collapsed "basket cases" (some even had huge trees growing through their roofs). Often it seems the worse they are, the more we want them.  Their former beauty shines through and their history speaks to us.
 You see, we think that the history and romanticism of New Orleans is best conveyed through the preservation and use of its unique architecture, cooking it's amazing food,  and playing it's fantastic music. And well, since we can't boil water or play a single instrument between us, we've decided to concentrate on the houses. We hope you like what we've done; it wasn't easy. You never know, maybe our daughter will grow up to be a chef who plays the clarinet.

name: Marigny Afterglow | Gaslit Stay Near Music & Food
description:
Welcome to The Marigny Afterglow, a historic gas-lit shotgun double in one of New Orleans’ most magical neighborhoods.

Restored with modern comforts, the home features 12-foot ceilings, original details, and a clawfoot tub for slow mornings and long soaks.

Steps from music on Frenchmen, an easy walk to the French Quarter, or stay close in the Marigny and Bywater for some of the city’s best food. As evening settles in, gaslights flicker outside.

Made for music, meals, and nights that linger.
host_about:
I've lived all over the country, from Kansas City to Cleveland, Vail Colorado to Nantucket, Minneapolis to Philadelphia, California to Atlanta but New Orleans...New Orleans is home.  I fell in love with the city in 2002 when visiting a friend that went to school at Tulane and came down every couple of years there after; I helped to rebuilt houses after Katrina in the Musicians Village, and moved down full time in 2015.  

It was 4 years ago I found my LOVE, a 150 year old Victorian Shotgun Double house in the Marigny, that I've been restoring ever since and I lovingly refer to it as my #neverendingproject.  

I love good food, a well made cocktail and the arts; I will happily make suggestions for your trip if desired. I will also do everything I can to make sure you get off the beaten tourist path so you can see the real New Orleans from the point of view of a local.
  
Bob Dylan says it best... 

"There are a lot of places I like, but I like New Orleans better... The city is one very long poem. Gardens full of pansies, pink petunias, opiates. Flower-bedecked shrines, white myrtles, bougainvillea and purple oleander stimulate your senses, make you feel cool and clear inside.”

 “Everything in New Orleans is a good idea".

Best, 
 
 - JPH

Ashley & Chris

New Orleans Restoration Properties, owned by Marcy and Paul, is a fourth generation full service real estate development company that specializes in the restoration of historic properties.

NOLA RP’s Mission is to contribute to the Revitalization of Historic Neighborhoods by providing high quality restored properties for consumers to participate in neighborhood redevelopment through the purchasing and renting of formerly blighted properties. We will continue to spark an urban renewal in the medium-lower income neighborhoods that encourages residents to invest in their community not only financially but also socially and culturally. We and our community partners unite our efforts to make New Orleans a better place to live. We will be a part of the solution for the city of New Orleans concerning the issues of blight and crime. We are now in the 5th generation of our family run business and the oldest oyster processors in the United States. Today I run the business with my brother Sal, and son Blake Sunseri. We're excited to welcome guests to our family business to share some of the rich culture and history the city has to offer.

name: Art Lovers Garden Hideaway in the  Riverbend
description: Beautiful suite with queen bed and bathroom with private entrance in artist home in the Historic Carrollton Riverbend neighborhood, off-street parking plus lovely garden great for enjoying morning coffee. 15 minute Uber/Lyft ride to Jazz Fest or French Quarter. Short walk to the our famous streetcar for a leisurely ride to Garden District or Quarter. Just blocks from lively Oak St. with great local restaurants, coffee shops, bars and music venues. Near Audubon Park, universities, and Ochsner.
host_about:
I was born and raised in this beautifully diverse and unique culture of New Orleans. I have worked as a fine art photographer, curator, teacher, travel photographer, and  author of  “Elysium, A Gathering of Souls, New Orleans Cemeteries” . My fine art photographs have been widely exhibited in the USA and abroad and have also appeared in Vogue, Elle, The Traveler and numerous publications on photography. My passions include art and culture, design, travel, especially Italy, France, Spain and gardens of all kinds and last but not least my wild and crazy hometown of New Orleans!! 

My husband and co-host, Evert,  grew up in Haarlem, The Netherlands and is an abstract painter. During a trip to the USA we met at a gallery in New Orleans. Evert returned to New Orleans as a visiting artist of painting and drawing at Loyola University and later he moved from Haarlem to New Orleans where we got married and now reside. Evert is regarded as an established New Orleans artist and represented by the Cole Pratt Gallery on Magazine St. Evert speaks Dutch and English of course but also a little German and French.

Evert and I have many of the same interests and both love welcoming visitors to New Orleans and sharing our recommendations for our favorite local places! Being a host is a great way to introduce new visitors to the real New Orleans and its many diverse neighborhoods, restaurants and events. As Hosts we are open, flexible and want to ensure that you have everything you need for a comfortable and memorable stay in New Orleans!

name: Summerland
description: Whether you’re looking for a romantic getaway, a peaceful weekend or a great location for exploring New Orleans, my house just might be perfect for you.  It is blocks from the French Quarter, music clubs on Frenchmen, St. Claude and others.  Enjoy a full kitchenette, queen bed, and high speed WiFi.  There are lots of coffee shops, cafes and restaurants close by, and there's great architecture everywhere you look!
host_about:
I had been coming to New Orleans since 1988, and it was constantly pulling me back. As a radio professional for over 40 years, I had for 7 consecutive years produced, engineered and hosted a live one and a-half-hour show in the Boston area that I innovated, and named “I Love A Parade!”

A parade of artists from all venues, musicians of all genres, and craftspeople all from many places came into the studio to play and converse about life, their artforms, on what they were currently working, music that inspires them, and a lot of laughs. I narrated all kinds of original, improvisational, and published writing, and shared all kinds of music - with an ear to theme and segue and mostly music from New Orleans! 

Friends were often asking me, “When are you moving to New Orleans?” ~ maybe ‘cuz of what I put out there, or that the show was named “I Love A Parade!” (A new similar podcast from the house is coming soon! Maybe you can be a part of it!”)!

With all this, I woke up one snowy day, covers clutched to my chin, and looking at the ceiling, said loudly, without hesitation, “I’m movin’ to New Orleans!!”

So I cleared out the house, sold it and my cars, loaded up my son’s car, called the dog into the backseat, and with my two cats, my son and all, drove down from Somerville, MA (the NOLA of the U.S. North) to New Orleans! So glad!

Since then, I bought a house and a car, and now Christy’s Place. We named it Summerland, and now I get to meet you! Fun!

name: Pet-Friendly Mid-City beauty near streetcar line!
description: Large, pet-friendly (all pets subject to approval & pet fee) 5BR/3BA home tucked between Mid-City, Bayou Saint John, and the Lafitte Greenway. Enjoy easy access to the red streetcar line for exploring City Park Ave and the French Quarter. Walking distance to the famous Parkway Tavern and Bayou Beer Garden, and minutes from the Fairgrounds. Relax in our spacious living areas or take a stroll through scenic trails - perfect for pets and families alike!
host_about:
We both were born and raised in New Orleans. New Orleanians embrace the term “Southern Hospitality.” New Orleans is a tourist/hospitality based economy, which is rich in southern culture; from the food, the history, the architecture, and most importantly, the people. 

Chris is a Real Estate Developer and Home Builder and he loves what he does! He loves to take old historic homes and bringing them back to life. And Ashley loves to manage, decorate these homes and mostly, communicate with our guests and making their stay as enjoyable as possible. The vacation rental business gives us the opportunity to share our home with not only locals in New Orleans but people around the world. New Orleans has some of the oldest homes in the country and there is a lot of history in each house! We look forward to sharing this history with our guests. 

When we’re not working, we enjoy the outdoors, traveling the world, spending time with our Golden Retriever, Amber and family and friends. Louisiana is known as “the Sportsman’s Paradise.” Chris loves to hunt and fish as well! We both are sports junkies. Chris is a HUGE LSU fan and funny thing…Ashley is a Bama fan…so house divided here! We both love Saints football as well!

We both love to entertain and we firmly believe by doing this, it provides a great opportunity to provide the best travel experience for our guests so much that we decided to share our home with our guests..that right there is Southern Hospitality at its finest! 
We look forward to hosting you in New Orleans!

Ashley & Chris

We both love to entertain and we firmly believe by doing this, it provides a great opportunity to provide the best travel experience for our guests so much that we decided to share our home with our guests..that right there is Southern Hospitality at its finest! 
We look forward to hosting you in New Orleans!

description:
We welcome all walks of life to this little piece of paradise and look forward to hosting you. Anytime Check In • FREE street parking • Fast Wifi • Electronic Locks

Built in the late 19th Century, this eclectic 3bd home has been restored and decorated to accommodate modern living while creating a mid century Bohemian charm in a historic colorful neighborhood.

host_about:
Hi, our profile name says Greg, but actually we are an easy going couple, Greg and Danielle that wants to meet you! 

You will be in good hands when you stay with us. Our travel and unique life experiences have taught us how to make you comfortable while traveling.

We have over 445 positive reviews on Air BnB, over 50 on Couchsurfing, and multiple others on HelpX and Workaway.  

You love to host, hopefully you will see this in our positive reviews.

A bit about us: In 2009 we quit our day jobs and spent the next for 2.5 years traveling full time. Landing in Miami, Florida in February of 2012, we hosted many in our tiny Condo. We moved to New Orleans in October of 2015 and spent the first year and a half renovating our dream home in this magical city. 

In 2019, the house next door came up for sale, and we purchased it in the middle of the Pandemic! We updated it, made it beautiful,  and now share it with travelers like you. We welcome all walks of life into our home. We look forward to meeting you! 

In almost a decade of extensive travel, we've built many friendships, discovered and learned more about ourselves, people and the world than we ever could have imagined. 

We have great history of hosting people in our temporary homes throughout the US and world.  We use Air BnB, and other websites/organizations to facilitate guests in our home. We enjoy Air BnB, and offer our guests a great experience. 

If you're interested in business and entrepreneurship, you will enjoy staying with us. Ask about our company Elektra Cosmetics, where our mission is to empower people by inspiring a community to be unapologetically creative. Through support, education and quality products we spread the joy of creativity. It has been exciting as we work to develop and grow our business. Just look up Elektra Cosmetics using your favorite search engine or social media platform to learn more.

We are computer geeks and internet junkies we love to utilize technology for learning, exploring, researching, completing tasks, and keeping in touch with friends and family.

We love all types food :). We are not foodies, just love trying new cuisines and restaurants. We try not to overindulge, but sharing conversation over a nice meal is always very nice.

We enjoy experiencing the sights and sounds of new locations. We have been on numerous walking and biking tours, and have walked many miles in each place we visit. We look forward to many more enjoyable walks in around our home we hope you can join us for a few. 

Danielle- I am the founder and creator of Beauty Butler Makeup Organizer. I am also a Certified Orthotist I specialize in designing and fitting helmets on infants with positional plagiocephaly...a condition where a baby's head is becomes abnormally flat from pressure. 

Danielle- My interests are decorating, exploring New Orleans, food, costumes, history, thrifting, vintage, art & adventure, and last but not least,  I love burlesque!!!! New Orleans is a city with a thriving burlesque and performance art community. There is almost a show or two every night of the week. 

Greg- I enjoy working with various forms of technology. Particularly productivity tools such as computers, the internet, mobile computing, applications and software. I am a smart phone junkie! Once I learn techniques and tips, sharing this information with others to help make their day to day routines easier is what I enjoy most. 

Greg- I am regularly working toward improving myself as a person. It is a great challenge, and helps me avoid boredom. I have come a long way, and can see there is a long way to go. I guess it would be called living life, and it is a great journey:)

description: Nestled in the vibrant heart of the Bywater, this charming 1 bed / 1 bath retreat offers the best of both worlds—just minutes from the French Quarter, yet tucked into one of New Orleans’ most beloved historic neighborhoods. host_about: I am originally from Italy and moved to New Orleans in 2017 after meeting my wife in Europe. My wife is originally from New Orleans and knows the city well, so we decided combine my passion for real estate and her passion for New Orleans to open our first Airbnb. host_about:
Let me take a moment and introduce myself.  My Name is Joan but my friends call me Joni or JJ. At one time, I was a Pastry Chef at the New Orleans Hilton Riverside.  I worked their for almost ten years.  I started their as a Culinary Apprentice while attending Delgado Community College and enrolled in the Culinary program.  In addition to attending classes, as a full time student, for three years, to include summers, I needed 6000 logged working hours to graduate.  After Graduation and studying under the famous Executive Pastry Chef George Cook, I was promoted to Assistant Pastry Chef.  I worked there for years and loved the artistry, my employees and the industry.  As all good things must come to an end, I left there to purchase a restaurant on Decatur Street.  Unfortunately, unforeseen complications occurred and I found myself unemployed.  So what did I do; I ended up spending a lot of time on a Florida beach. I was young, care free and needed time to evaluate my situation over Pina Colada's. I bounced around until I realized I should have a better understanding of the Bar Business. It was my goal to own and operate a Restuarant and Bar but in my case, a Bar that features live music with a limited Grub Menu.  It appeared to be the only logical path I should travel.  With that said, I started working as a bartender at Bank Street Bar and Deckbar & Grill.  My plan was moving along and everything was great for many years..  Then K-a-t-r-i-n-a happened and destroyed the life we once new.  Any hoot, Moving forward,  all of my work experiences lead me to becoming a  part owner and operator in Legends Bar & Grill;  until, It wasn't anymore. That is a whole other story that I will not get into but it is a bitter sweet memory and I have to say "I am who I am today" because of the good, the bad and the ugly that has occured.  Which leads me to the here and now. For the past twelve years, I have worked as a Dock Operator on the Mississippi River and my present goal is to become a Super Host with Air BnB... 
Please join me in my journey in becoming a "Super Host".

name: Steps from Audubon Park & Magazine St Amenities
description:
Steps from Audubon Park and Magazine St. shops and restaurants, this 1 bedroom apartment has a generously sized living area and a spacious bedroom.

Audubon Park anchors the neighborhood and is a great spot to enjoy a bike ride, a quiet walk, a round of golf, a picnic, or a little sunshine on the banks of the Mississippi.

The house is located within stumbling distance of Uptown Amenities that include grocers, restaurants, watering holes, shopping, coffee shops, and Mardi Gras Parades.
host_about:
I moved to New Orleans in 1993 to attend Tulane University.  And the City that Care Forgot wasted no time sucking me in.  As a young man, my Uptown neighborhood met my every want and need - a half block from Mardi Gras, a quick stumble to some of the best live music in the city at Tipitina's and Les Bons Temps, fine eats at Dick and Jenny's, and plenty of libations within striking distance.  Now I am older, with three children, and though my needs have changed the neighborhood still provides - ice cream at Creole Creamery, snowballs at Hansen's Sno-Bliz, two playgrounds, a children's library, and pizza.  And of course Mardi Gras.

I have moved three times in the last 15 years.  Never more than 6 blocks.

The Inn features beautiful molding, 12' ceilings, a lovely light filled living room and dining room, a modern kitchen, front and back porch, onsite parking, huge backyard, and our own blend of artsy charm. The inn has 6 bedrooms and this listing is for one with a private bath down the hall. We also offer rooms with attached bathrooms and suites, search The Okra Inn to find our other offerings.
host_about:
Hi all!  

We're Lindsay, Adam, Penny and David. Lindsay is a fifth generation New Orleanian, and Penny and David are sixth generation. Lindsay started The Okra Inn in 2014 and now it's a family business, hosting group stays and individual guests at two locations in Mid-City, New Orleans.

Thanks for looking at The Okra Inn! If you'd like more information, send a message. We look forward to having you!

host_about:
I love traveling the world, particularly Latin America.  I have an affection for things leather-bound, rustic, old, or filled with character.  I am always happy to pass up on modern conveniences.  Triathlon enthusiast.

Favorite places to visit in the United States:  Provincetown, Massachusetts;  Asheville, North Carolina;  New Orleans, Louisiana;  Big Sur, California.  Favorite places to visit in the world:  Mexico, Argentina, Ecuador, Italy, Tunisia, and Vietnam.

Favorite wines:  Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Valpolicella Ripasso, Montepulciano d'Abruzzo.

My favorite poem - "If" by Rudyard Kipling:
If you can keep your head when all about you   
    Are losing theirs and blaming it on you,   
If you can trust yourself when all men doubt you,
    But make allowance for their doubting too;   
If you can wait and not be tired by waiting,
    Or being lied about, don’t deal in lies,
Or being hated, don’t give way to hating,
    And yet don’t look too good, nor talk too wise:

If you can dream—and not make dreams your master;   
    If you can think—and not make thoughts your aim;   
If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster
    And treat those two impostors just the same;   
If you can bear to hear the truth you’ve spoken
    Twisted by knaves to make a trap for fools,
Or watch the things you gave your life to, broken,
    And stoop and build ’em up with worn-out tools:

If you can make one heap of all your winnings
    And risk it on one turn of pitch-and-toss,
And lose, and start again at your beginnings
    And never breathe a word about your loss;
If you can force your heart and nerve and sinew
    To serve your turn long after they are gone,   
And so hold on when there is nothing in you
    Except the Will which says to them: ‘Hold on!’

If you can talk with crowds and keep your virtue,   
    Or walk with Kings—nor lose the common touch,
If neither foes nor loving friends can hurt you,
    If all men count with you, but none too much;
If you can fill the unforgiving minute
    With sixty seconds’ worth of distance run,   
Yours is the Earth and everything that’s in it,   
    And—which is more—you’ll be a Man, my son!

host_about: I am a retired Social Worker and a New Orleans native. I have resided in my home since 1943. My home was one of the first home in the Treme area dated 1836. The layout in the home provides two bedrooms and  two private bathrooms. It also has double winding stair cases with an Angel Cloud mural ceiling that leads to the   second and third floors. The common area has two six-foot water fountains, two fire places, plants and artwork. This area promotes a calm relaxing atmosphere to plan your day or simply relax.
